item.title: No surrender, no dissent: How six months of war hardened Iran’s leadership
item.description: Iran's leadership has appointed hard-line military and security officials to key positions. These moves signal a resistance to US pressure and a crackdown on domestic dissent. The new appointments come as Iran faces prolonged confrontation and economic pressure. Hardliners are tightening their grip around the new supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei. This consolidation aims to maintain unity and prepare for potential unrest and further conflict.
item.dc:creator: Vijaya Srivastava

item.title: McDonald's-backed grants unlock $99.1m for conservation across 100,650 US acres
item.description: McDonald's and its partners are actively funding conservation easements throughout the United States. With these grants, they will preserve over 100,000 acres of essential grasslands, providing support for ranching communities and a variety of wildlife. The initiative seeks to secure important habitats and migration paths for numerous species while promoting sustainable practices in beef cattle production.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Three forgotten kings may change the accepted timeline of ancient Assyria
item.description: Research indicates that ancient Assyrian king lists could have neglected to mention several ephemeral rulers. Evidence points to three monarchs who temporarily ascended the throne amid turbulent political times. Their short reigns might have been intentionally omitted from the official historical timeline, raising questions about the accuracy of Assyria's established chronology.

item.title: A wooden relic that survived the sack of Jerusalem's First Temple was unearthed by archaeologists, now they are finding shocking answers
item.description: In a remarkable find, archaeologists uncovered ancient wooden beams from the destruction of Jerusalem's First Temple, dating back over 2,600 years to 586 B.C. These preserved sycamore beams, covered in melted plaster, are believed to have supported the roof of an inner courtyard. By analyzing the growth rings, researchers have accurately dated this crucial archaeological evidence, providing an extraordinary link to Jerusalem's rich and ancient history.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Scientists spent 100 years discovering animals, reshaping where we see Earth’s biodiversity hotspots
item.description: A groundbreaking study has unveiled that taxonomic advancements have reshaped worldwide biodiversity maps over the last century. While reptile and amphibian diversity has markedly changed, bird and mammal distributions have remained mostly unchanged. Australia and Southeast Asia have been identified as key biodiversity hotspots for these groups. Moreover, factors influencing species richness are also shifting, with precipitation emerging as more crucial.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: In 2002, Alabama architecture students stacked 72,000 worn carpet tiles into the walls of a family home
item.description: Students at Rural Studio have transformed donated carpet tiles into the innovative Lucy Carpet House, providing a vital home and prayer space for the Harris family. This initiative is part of a broader effort that has resulted in over 200 projects within Hale County, enabling students to gain hands-on experience while tackling the challenges of affordable housing in rural communities.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: They were digging a sewer when they found gold worth $10.4M
item.description: While digging trenches for a new sewage system in Belgium, construction workers stumbled upon an astonishing treasure worth over ten million dollars. This remarkable find consisted of various gold bars and coins. Authorities have secured the precious haul in a high-security federal vault, adhering to Belgian regulations that permit rightful owners a five-year window to claim their treasure.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A former Illinois school is now a $1.35M accessible park with an inclusive playground and splash pad
item.description: On August 26, Galesburg proudly unveiled Cooke Park, a fully accessible neighborhood space built on the site of the former Cooke Elementary School. This ambitious $1.352 million project features an inclusive playground and splash pad, showcasing the community's dedication to inclusivity. The ribbon-cutting ceremony was attended by local officials and community leaders, marking a significant partnership between the government and residents.

item.title: Rakshabandhan in NYC: Zohran Mamdani celebrates with South Asian seniors
item.description: During a heartfelt celebration of Rakshabandhan at India Home, NYC mayor Zohran Mamdani emphasized the festival's profound themes of protection, support, and unity. Drawing parallels to the rakhi's significance, he reaffirmed his dedication to ensuring the welfare of all New Yorkers. The mayor commended India Home for nurturing a sense of community and belonging among seniors, encouraging residents to foster these values citywide.
item.dc:creator: Vijaya Srivastava

item.title: US to establish first space academy, expand "far beyond the Moon"
item.description: President Trump has taken a monumental step by signing an order to create America's inaugural space academy, designed to elevate the nation's future leaders in space exploration. In a momentous interaction, he engaged with astronauts on the International Space Station. This initiative follows prior plans for lunar missions and commercial ventures, culminating in the recognition of the Artemis II crew with the prestigious Congressional Space Medal of Honour.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: In 2024, a Minnesota dairy began turning manure from more than 2,000 cows into renewable gas
item.description: In Minnesota, a pioneering dairy farm is transforming cow manure into ultra-low-carbon fuel for vehicles. This innovative facility processes thousands of gallons of manure each day, producing biomethane that enters interstate natural gas pipelines. By capturing methane—a significant greenhouse gas—before it escapes into the atmosphere, this project not only aids the environment but also provides a vital income stream for local dairy farmers.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Las Vegas Valley converted 250 million sq ft of lawn to save water, saving 203 billion gallons
item.description: Las Vegas is making headlines for its initiative to remove grass lawns, which has successfully conserved billions of gallons of water. Nevertheless, this environmental strategy has led to a concerning increase in local summer land-surface temperatures, soaring by around 20 degrees Celsius. As a response, water agencies are now promoting the use of water-efficient landscaping and shade trees, and new guidelines prevent grass installations in residential yards.
